---
title: Customized Modules
---

Add an extension at the narrowest interface that owns the new behavior. This
keeps provider transport, model formatting, retrieval, and tool presentation
independently testable.

### Choose an extension point

| Need | Extend |
| --- | --- |
| Call another model API | `searcherkit.llm.Client` |
| Support another model chat or tool format | `searcherkit.llm.parsers.Parser` |
| Search or fetch from another backend | `searcherkit.sources.DataSource` |
| Expose another model-callable action | `searcherkit.tools.BaseTool` |
| Add dataset or index deployment logic | `searcherkit.plugins` |
| Add a batch or training integration | `searcherkit.runtime` or `searcherkit.training` |

Do not place provider HTTP calls in parsers, retrieval code in CLI commands, or
benchmark-specific implementation in packaged config defaults.

### Construction contract

Public runtime components should support normal Python parameters and their
structured config or factory path. A custom source or tool can be selected with
`type: custom` and a real import target:

```yaml
agent:
  sources:
    - type: custom
      name: internal_corpus
      target: pkg://my_project.sources:InternalSource
  tools:
    - type: custom
      name: lookup
      target: pkg://my_project.tools:LookupTool
      extra:
        source_name: internal_corpus
```

`pkg://` targets resolve an installed Python module in the form
`pkg://package.module:attribute`. `file://` targets load a Python file and use
the form `file:///absolute/path/module.py:attribute`. A custom source receives
`SourceConfig`; a custom tool receives `ToolConfig`, and fields under `extra`
are passed as additional keyword arguments.

### Custom source

Implement the three asynchronous `DataSource` operations. `search` returns
ranked `SearchResult` values, `fetch` returns a complete `Document`, and
`close` releases clients and connection pools:

```python
from searcherkit.sources import DataSource, Document, SearchResult, SourceConfig

class InternalSource(DataSource):
    def __init__(self, *, config: SourceConfig) -> None:
        self.endpoint = config.client_kwargs["endpoint"]
        self.client = make_client(self.endpoint)

    async def search(self, query: str, *, top_k: int = 10) -> list[SearchResult]:
        rows = await self.client.search(text=query, limit=top_k)
        return [
            SearchResult(
                document=Document(id=str(row["id"]), title=row.get("title"),
                                  text=row["text"], url=row.get("url")),
                score=float(row["score"]) if row.get("score") is not None else None,
                snippet=row.get("snippet"),
            )
            for row in rows
        ]

    async def fetch(self, document_id: str, *, goal: str | None = None) -> Document:
        row = await self.client.fetch(document_id)
        return Document(id=str(row["id"]), title=row.get("title"), text=row["text"])

    async def close(self) -> None:
        await self.client.close()
```

### Custom tool

Subclass `BaseTool` and implement `_run`. Tool metadata and the JSON schema can
be inferred from the signature or specified in configuration:

```python
from searcherkit.tools import BaseTool, ToolConfig
from searcherkit.sources import build_source

class LookupTool(BaseTool):
    def __init__(self, *, config: ToolConfig, source_name: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(config=config)
        self.source = build_source(source_name)

    async def _run(self, *, query: str, limit: int = 5) -> tuple[str, dict[str, object]]:
        results = await self.source.search(query, top_k=limit)
        content = "\n\n".join(
            f"[{item.document.id}] {item.document.title or ''}\n{item.document.text}"
            for item in results
        )
        return content, {"result_count": len(results)}

    async def close(self) -> None:
        await self.source.close()
```

The corresponding `extra.source_name` is passed to the constructor. Use
`argument_mapping` when the model-facing argument name differs from the Python
parameter name.

### Test the contract

Extension tests should cover, when applicable:

1. construction through direct parameters and through config or factory paths;
2. functional inputs, outputs, payloads, parsing, state, and public errors;
3. retry success after transient failures and final error propagation after all
   attempts fail;
4. resource initialization and shutdown.

Catch concrete exception types and classify failures as recoverable or fatal at
the boundary where that distinction is known.

For config, CLI, recipe, or plugin entry-point changes, also run a compose,
`--help`, or import check in addition to targeted tests. Keep the API Reference
accurate by updating Google-style docstrings on the public implementation.
